_: MEASURED LIFT PER NAMED STRUCTURE. This file is the ONLY authority on what a structure has been measured to do; `base_catalog.Structure` deliberately carries no lift field, so the catalog can never disagree with the harness. `published: false` means we have no number -- either it was never measured or it was measured and refused -- and `base_catalog.meta()` surfaces None for both, because to a member they say the same honest thing. The reasons stay here for anyone auditing.
method: Lift = conditional rate - pattern-free rate, where the pattern-free half is restricted to the YEARS the structure actually fired in (the baseline drifts: target-first ran 17.1% in 2018 and 35.7% in 2020). Anchors are stepped by the full 20-session horizon so no two observations share a forward window. The CI is a 400-draw CLUSTER BOOTSTRAP resampling tickers with replacement, because detections cluster by ticker and a two-proportion SE assumes that away. The null re-runs the IDENTICAL detector over MOVING-BLOCK resampled series (21-bar blocks) so local volatility clustering survives and only the long-range order is destroyed -- an iid shuffle would hand a quiet-regime detector a free volatility premium.
gates: SIX gates, and all must pass or NO number is published. (0) THE LIFT MUST BE POSITIVE. This gate was missing and it FIRED: `cheat-3c` measured -1.10pp with a CI of [-2.16, -0.09] against a null max of -3.91pp and published, because its interval excludes zero (both bounds negative) and its lower bound clears a null that is even more negative. A structure that reliably UNDERPERFORMS its own baseline was surfaced to members as a measured edge. A negative result is a finding and stays here with its reasons; it is not a lift to put in front of anyone. (1) The lift's 95% CI excludes zero. (2) The CI's LOWER BOUND exceeds the random-data null's maximum -- not the point estimate, which let a +32.97pp lift on n=13 through on the first run. (3) n is whatever (1) requires, derived rather than typed. AND A PUBLISHED ROW MUST CARRY 30 NULL TRIALS, not the 5 used to screen: the null's maximum can only grow with more draws, so a small trial count is a strictly easier gate and would be a dial pointing at publication. The escalation has changed a verdict in BOTH directions -- stage-4-breakdown passed at 30 after failing at 5 on a narrower sample, and buyable-gap-up failed at 30 after passing at 5. (4) THE SAME-DATE CLUSTERING MUST HAVE BEEN MEASURED, and gates 1 and 2 are applied to the interval WIDENED by it. The bootstrap behind every interval resamples TICKERS, so it is blind to a structure firing on hundreds of different names on one day -- one market event, not hundreds of observations -- and the interval it returns is too narrow. Measured within-date correlation runs 0.13 to 0.35 across these rows, a design effect up to 7.11, so an interval widens by as much as 2.67x. A row whose clustering has never been measured is REFUSED rather than published on the narrow bound: half the noise term missing is not a smaller claim, it is an unfounded one. This gate cost two rows that had cleared the other four -- square-box and low-cheat. ⭐ AND IT WIDENS BY RHO'S UPPER BOUND, NOT ITS POINT ESTIMATE, for the same reason gate 2 reads the CI's lower bound rather than the point: the pessimistic end is the honest one. Rho is bootstrapped over whole DATES, since the date is the cluster. Measured 2026-09-01 this changed NO verdict -- every published row clears its null on rho's upper bound too -- which is the robustness result, not a reason the gate should have used the looser number. (5) THE STRUCTURE MUST MAKE MONEY ON THE METRIC IT IS GRADED WITH. Lift is a difference of WIN RATES against a pattern-free baseline, and a structure can beat that baseline while losing money on the bracket the lift was measured with. Grimes and Brandt independently call the win rate the wrong headline number, and they are right: this gate fired on two rows that had cleared all five others.
sample: Seeded-random draw from the screener universe, up to 3,000 daily bars per ticker. The size differs per structure and per run, so it is recorded on each row as `sample_tickers` rather than claimed once here; a row's window is `tools/run_lift_ledger.py::WINDOWS[key]`.
baseline_metric: P(+10% before -8% within 20 sessions). Measured unconditionally over the whole 3,705-name universe by an independent code path: 27.51% target-first, 33.41% stop-first, 39.08% neither. The per-structure pattern-free baselines below came out at 27.01-28.71%, which is the cross-check that this harness measures what it claims to.
limitations:
⚠️ A PREDICTION IN THIS FIELD WAS FALSIFIED BY THE DATA, and the correction matters more than the original claim. It read: 'widening the sample can tighten an estimate but not flip its sign.' The full-universe re-measure flipped two. `cup-with-handle` went from -7.18pp on 279 tickers -- where I wrote a confident note explaining why the most famous base in the industry sat below its own null -- to -0.18pp with an interval straddling zero on 3,408: a NON-EVENT, and the small-sample negative was noise. `square-box` went the other way, from an interval straddling zero to a published +0.99pp. Sign stability under resampling is not something a narrow sample entitles you to assume.

(1) SAMPLE -- now the full universe. Every row was re-measured on 3,456 tickers (those carrying enough history for its window), not the 279 the first pass used. Each row still records its own `sample_tickers`, since the usable count differs by window. This was run ONCE and its output stands, including for structures that came back worse; re-running at successively wider samples until a structure passes would be p-hacking with extra steps.

(2) NULL DEPTH -- `null_trials` is part of every verdict, not a footnote to it. A row refused at 5 trials was refused by a null that could only get WEAKER with fewer draws, so its refusal is safe. A row PUBLISHED at fewer than 30 is not, which is why every published row carries 30 and a rail enforces it.

(3) DIRECTION -- the metric is P(+10% before -8%), a LONG outcome, and it is applied to every structure regardless of bias. For a BEARISH structure a positive lift therefore says price resolved UPWARD more often than baseline, which is an oversold-bounce reading rather than confirmation the structure works. `stage-4-breakdown` publishes +7.30pp under exactly that reading. The number is real; the interpretation is not the obvious one, and a directional metric per bias is the honest next step.

(4) IMPLEMENTATION SUBSETS -- several detectors are explicitly narrower than the rule they name, and each says so on its criteria: the buyable gap-up omits a volume gate whose two published phrasings differ by a factor of 1.67; the pocket pivot omits a fundamentals gate that is not computable from bars; the saucer is measured on daily bars although its house says the pattern is 'only visible on a weekly or monthly chart'. A gate not applied is a rejection not made, so those rows include names the full rule would refuse.

⛔⛔ MULTIPLE COMPARISONS: MEASURED AS A BOUND, NOT CORRECTED. Twenty-five structures carry a measured null and several are graded in both directions, so the family here is roughly thirty tests. Each published row's gate 1 asks only whether ITS OWN interval excludes zero, and that question means considerably less asked thirty times than once. No family-wise correction is applied.

A CRUDE UPPER BOUND ON THE CORRECTION, computable from what is stored: the largest null maximum anywhere in the ledger is +18.92pp (parabolic-extension). Under a Westfall-Young style rule that compares each result to the distribution of the family's MAXIMUM, a bar at that level is cleared by only 1 of the 5 published rows -- parabolic-extension (clustered CI low +25.85pp). climax-top, darvas-box, ema-crossback, stage-4-breakdown fall below it.

⚠️ RE-DERIVED 2026-09-01 AGAINST THE CLUSTERED BOUNDS, and the answer moved. This paragraph previously named climax-top as clearing the bar at +19.08pp. That was its TICKER-ONLY bootstrap bound; widened for its measured same-date design effect it reads +18.61pp and no longer clears. Two corrections that are each individually survivable are not jointly survivable, and a note stating one of them in terms of a bound the other has since moved is the stale-count defect this file keeps re-committing.

⚠️ THAT BOUND OVERSTATES THE CORRECTION, AND THE REASON MATTERS. Null maxima here are RAW lifts, and each detector has its own mechanical edge on random data: parabolic-extension's null reaches +18.92pp while darvas-box's reaches +1.10pp. Taking a maximum across detectors therefore mixes 'this particular detector drifts a lot on noise' with 'the family had many chances to get lucky', and only the second is multiplicity. A correct maxT is computed on statistics STANDARDISED by each structure's own null, over shared shuffles -- which needs the per-trial null VECTORS, and until 2026-09-01 the artifact retained only each row's maximum. Rows written from now on carry `null_lifts`, so the correction becomes computable without re-measuring everything.

⭐ WHAT TO TAKE FROM THIS TODAY. The true correction sits somewhere between 'none' and the bound above, and its size is UNKNOWN. Rows whose margin over their own null is large -- parabolic-extension +10.22pp, darvas-box +5.68pp -- have the most room to survive it. The three thinnest, low-cheat (+0.43pp), stage-4 (+1.06pp) and square-box (+1.16pp), have the least, and should be read as provisional until the family-wise question is settled rather than bounded.

⛔⛔ SURVIVORSHIP: STRUCTURAL, UNQUANTIFIED, AND NOT WHERE YOU WOULD FIRST LOOK. Measured 2026-09-01.

THE OBVIOUS SUSPECT IS INNOCENT. `load_universe` reads tickers at the latest `snapshot_date`, so a name whose row stopped being rebuilt is skipped. That sounds like the bias -- and it is 7 tickers out of 3,714, 0.2% of the table. Negligible. Anyone auditing this should stop looking there.

THE REAL BIAS IS UPSTREAM AND LARGER. Membership comes from `api/data/cap_universe.json`: a static, git-tracked list of 3,742 tickers that NOTHING IN THE REPO WRITES -- there is no generator, no refresh, no recorded as-of date. It is a roster of companies that exist NOW, and the bars behind every measurement reach back 3,000 sessions, roughly twelve years. Every company that listed and then disappeared inside that window is absent from the sample entirely, along with its whole price history. No anchor was ever drawn from it.

⚠️ THE DIRECTION IS NOT CLEAN, AND SAYING IT IS WOULD BE THE EASY MISTAKE. Delisting is not one event. A company acquired at a premium leaves the roster after a move that is a WIN on the long metric; a company that fails leaves after a move that is a LOSS on the long metric and a WIN on the short. Excluding both removes wins AND losses from both arms, and which dominates depends on the M&A-versus-failure mix over those twelve years -- a number this repo does not hold. So the sign of the bias on any given row is genuinely unknown, not merely unmeasured.

⭐ WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a point-in-time constituent list -- who was listed on each historical date -- which nothing here can derive from a roster that carries no date and no history. Until one exists, every lift in this file describes the structure's behaviour AMONG COMPANIES THAT SURVIVED TO TODAY, which is a narrower claim than it looks, and the narrowing is not symmetric across the long and short rows.

⛔⛔ SAME-DATE CLUSTERING: MEASURED, AND IT COST TWO ROWS. Measured 2026-09-01 over 650 tickers.

THE HOLE. Every interval in this file comes from a cluster bootstrap that resamples TICKERS. That is correct for one axis -- one ticker's anchors are not independent of each other -- and silent about the other: when a structure fires on hundreds of DIFFERENT names on the SAME DAY, those anchors share one market event and are not hundreds of observations. The bootstrap cannot see that, so the interval it returns is too NARROW, and gates 1 and 2 both read an interval's bound. Every check in the repo agreed with the bootstrap because every check asked the bootstrap.

⭐ IT WAS MEASURED, NOT BRACKETED. The tempting move is to assume a plausible within-date correlation and publish a range. The outcomes are on file, so instead the within-date intra-class correlation of the win/loss outcome was computed directly (one-way random effects, unequal clusters), giving a design effect deff = 1 + (m_eff - 1) * rho by which the true variance exceeds the bootstrap's; an interval's half-width scales with its square root. Across the rows that were published, rho ran 0.130 (ema-crossback) to 0.351 (parabolic-extension), and the largest design effect was 7.11 (stage-4-breakdown) -- an interval 2.67x wider than the one the bootstrap reported. The correlation is real and large; it is not a rounding concern.

⛔ CONSEQUENCE, NAMED: 2 of 7 previously published rows no longer clear their gates -- low-cheat (bound +0.83pp -> +0.38pp against a null of +0.40pp); square-box (bound +0.35pp -> -0.29pp against a null of -0.81pp). The remaining 5 stand: climax-top, darvas-box, ema-crossback, parabolic-extension, stage-4-breakdown.

⚠️ WHAT THE CORRECTION DOES NOT COVER, PRECISELY. A lift is a difference of two rates, and rho was measured on the CONDITIONAL ARM only -- the anchors where the structure fired. That arm carries the smaller n and therefore most of the variance, so this is the dominant term rather than an exact recomputation of the interval. The clustering is also measured on the SAME 20-bar stepped anchor grid the bootstrap resampled, so it describes the sample these intervals were actually built from; a denser grid would find more same-day overlap, not less. Read the corrected bounds as the honest reading of these numbers, not as a second published estimate.

⭐ STANDING RULE FROM HERE: a row may publish only with a MEASURED design effect. `adjudicate` refuses a row without one rather than falling back to the narrow bound -- half the noise term missing is not a smaller claim, it is an unfounded one. The provenance is `docs/base_lift_clustering.json`; the gate is `lift_ledger.clustered_bounds`.

⭐⭐ IS THIS LEDGER FINISHED? FOR NULL TRIALS, YES, AND THAT IS PROVABLE RATHER THAN ASSERTED. Derived 2026-09-01.

15 of 25 rows were graded against only 5 null trials, well under the 30 a published row requires, so the obvious remaining work is to escalate them. It is futile, and the reason is structural rather than empirical: a null MAXIMUM can only GROW as trials are added, so gate 2 -- the CI's lower bound must exceed that maximum -- gets strictly HARDER with every trial. A row failing it at 5 fails it at 30. Gate 0 (the lift must be positive) and gate 1 (the interval must exclude zero) do not read the null at all, so no number of trials touches them either.

⛔ CHECKED ROW BY ROW, NOT ARGUED: applying gates 0, 1 and 2 to every unpublished measured row -- on its CLUSTERED bound where one exists -- leaves ZERO rows an escalation could rescue. All 25 measured rows are therefore at their final verdict, and the library stands at 5 published.

⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. It forecloses more NULL TRIALS, not more DATA. A larger ticker sample would move `lift` and tighten `ci_low`, and that could change a verdict in either direction -- it is a different re-run, and this ledger's `sample_tickers` records what each row actually saw. Nor does it foreclose a detector CHANGE: a structure whose definition moves is a new measurement, not a re-grade of this one.

⭐ HOW MUCH WOULD THE CORRELATION HAVE TO MOVE? Derived 2026-09-01. For each published row there is a rho* at which its interval stops clearing its own null:

    structure              rho   rho 95% hi    rho*
    climax-top           0.149        0.255   1.781
    darvas-box           0.179        0.217   4.774
    ema-crossback        0.130        0.171   1.121
    parabolic-extension  0.351        0.582   2.107
    stage-4-breakdown    0.222        0.270   0.299

Four of the five have a rho* ABOVE 1.0 -- above the largest value a correlation can take -- so no clustering measurement, however wrong, could unpublish them. Their verdicts do not depend on this estimate at all.

⛔ STAGE-4-BREAKDOWN IS THE EXCEPTION AND SHOULD BE READ AS ONE. It flips at rho = 0.299 against a measured 0.222, and its 95% upper bound is 0.270 -- it survives with 0.03 of correlation to spare. It is published because it clears every gate on the conservative bound, and it is the one row whose publication a re-measurement could plausibly reverse.

⛔⛔ THE SHAPES ARE NOT RARE, AND THAT IS MEASURED. Measured 2026-09-01 over 417 tickers, 3 shuffled passes.

The research corpus calls this the highest-value non-obvious build in its whole methodology file: "for every pattern you ship, publish hits_real / hits_simulated. If it is near 1.0, the predicate is describing the noise process, not the market." We had shipped only half of it -- the null compared OUTCOMES, never FIRING RATES.

    structure               real      noise   ratio
    darvas-box             6.6091%   7.9811%    0.83
    stage-4-breakdown      9.2023%   10.2553%    0.90
    ema-crossback          5.2909%   5.8023%    0.91
    climax-top             1.9747%   2.0889%    0.94
    parabolic-extension    0.5107%   0.3688%    1.39

⛔ FOUR OF THE FIVE FIRE NO MORE OFTEN ON THE MARKET THAN ON A SHUFFLE, and three fire LESS. The null is a moving-block bootstrap: it keeps each stock's own return distribution AND its volatility clustering, and destroys only the long-range order -- which is the thing these detectors claim to read. So the shapes do not require the structure they are named for. A Darvas box is not a rare formation; a series with no long-range order produces them 21% MORE often.

⭐ WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT OVERTURN, PRECISELY. It does NOT invalidate the measured lifts: those compare outcomes AFTER the shape against pattern-free anchors in the same years, and a common shape can still be followed by a different outcome distribution. It DOES retire one reading of this library -- that these detectors find rare, distinctive formations. They do not. Whatever edge survives the gates lives entirely in WHAT FOLLOWS the shape in a real market, never in the shape being unusual. Any member-facing language implying rarity is unsupported.

⚠️ PARABOLIC-EXTENSION IS THE ONE EXCEPTION at 1.38 -- it fires 38% more often on real data than on a series with the same volatility and no memory, which is what a detector reading genuine momentum should look like. It is also the row with the largest margin over its own null. Those two facts agreeing is the only place in this file where the shape and the outcome tell the same story.

⛔⛔ TWO PUBLISHED ROWS LOST MONEY, AND EVERY OTHER GATE PASSED THEM. Measured 2026-09-01 over 417 tickers.

    structure                win%    stop%   unres%      E(R)     E(%)  trades/yr
    parabolic-extension     62.2%   34.1%    3.7%   +0.436   +3.49%     0.1
    darvas-box              34.4%   38.9%   26.7%   +0.081   +0.65%     0.7
    ema-crossback           40.6%   46.9%   12.5%   +0.046   +0.37%     0.6
    climax-top              41.2%   55.1%    3.7%   -0.036   -0.29%     0.2
    stage-4-breakdown       26.9%   44.4%   28.7%   -0.099   -0.79%     1.0

E(R) is expectancy per trade in units of the stop distance (8%). The bracket is 10%/8% over 20 bars, gross of all costs. `breakeven_roundtrip_pct` on each row is the round-trip cost at which the edge reaches zero -- reported instead of a guessed cost, so a reader can compare it against what they actually pay.

⛔ `stage-4-breakdown` WINS 3.30pp MORE OFTEN THAN ITS BASELINE AND LOSES 0.79% PER TRADE. Its win rate is 26.9% on a bracket that needs roughly 44% to break even. `climax-top` is the same story at -0.29%. Both cleared gates 0-4 -- positive lift, interval excluding zero, lower bound over the null at 30 trials, clustering measured -- and both are now REFUSED by gate 5. A member reading "+3.30pp" would have shorted it and lost.

⭐ THIS IS GATE 0'S ARGUMENT REACHED BY A DIFFERENT ROUTE. Gate 0 exists because a structure underperforming its own baseline is not a lift to put in front of a member. A structure that BEATS its baseline and still loses money is the same harm; the lift is true and the trade is not.

⚠️ THE BRACKET IS OURS. TARGET_PCT, STOP_PCT and HORIZON_BARS are origin: uct, not sourced from any authority, and a structure negative here could be positive on a different bracket -- a wider stop, a longer hold, a trailing exit. That is a real limitation and it is not a reason to publish the lift anyway: the lift is measured ON this bracket, so a lift and an expectancy from different brackets would describe different strategies. Re-measure both together or neither.

⭐⭐ THE BASE-STAGE DEGRADATION CURVE IBD NEVER PUBLISHED, MEASURED. 2026-09-01, 464 tickers, 900-bar tail, stage read CAUSALLY at each anchor.

    structure             early 1-2        late 3+     delta
    ema-crossback      44.8% (n=511)   26.3% (n=76)  +18.5pp
    darvas-box         35.8% (n=593)   37.1% (n=35)   -1.4pp
    parabolic-extension 46.0% (n=63)   50.0% (n=4)   not measurable

IBD asserts the preference four ways -- "usually best", "tend to be risky", "tend to produce larger gains", "seldom a charm" -- and quantifies it zero times. Measured on our universe the answer is STRUCTURE-DEPENDENT, which is not what a blanket rule predicts.

⛔ ema-crossback DEGRADES SHARPLY AND darvas-box DOES NOT. +18.5pp sits against a standard error of about 5.5pp, so it is real; darvas's -1.4pp sits against about 8.3pp and is indistinguishable from zero -- and it points the WRONG WAY for IBD's rule. parabolic-extension had four late-stage anchors, which is not a measurement and is reported as such rather than as 50%.

⭐ SO THE STAGE FILTER IS NOT APPLIED GLOBALLY, and that is the decision this measurement supports. IBD publishes no per-stage expectancy, so the stage was never usable as a weight; this shows it is not usable as a universal filter either. It belongs where it has been measured to matter.

⚠️ TWO LIMITS ON THIS NUMBER. The late-stage buckets are small (35 and 76), so only the ema-crossback gap is resolvable at all. And the tail was 900 bars per ticker, which gives the counter less history than a full series -- that biases stages LOW, pushing some genuinely late bases into the early bucket and, if anything, UNDERSTATING a real degradation.

+7.35pp, CI [+6.78pp, +7.96pp] at n=24,428, against a 30-trial null whose maximum reached +1.10pp.

The first structure to publish and the only one that has now cleared the bar on two independent samples. A 1960s box-range rule outscoring every modern base in this library is not the result anyone expected, and it is worth saying why it is credible: the moving-block null was built specifically to strip out the volatility premium a box detector would earn by selecting quiet stretches, and it removed almost nothing. ⛔ The structure ALSO carries our own recency bound: without it the label matched 96.7% of the universe, because over 400 bars nearly every stock frames a box at some point. The published number belongs to the gated definition, not to 'a Darvas box existed here once'.

stage-4-breakdown.note:
+3.30pp, CI [+2.78pp, +3.79pp] at n=34,216, against a 30-trial null whose maximum reached +1.72pp. Graded SHORT.

⭐⭐ THIS ROW IS WHY THE METRIC WAS FIXED, AND IT IS THE CLEAREST EVIDENCE THE FIX MATTERED. It once published +7.30pp -- graded LONG, as every structure was until the direction correction. On a long metric a positive lift says price resolved UPWARD after the breakdown, which is the opposite of the claim the structure's own name makes, so the number was more than twice as large AND answered the wrong question. Graded in the direction it actually claims, the honest answer is +3.30pp. The detector never changed; the question did.

⛔ A PUBLISHED SHORT LIFT IS NOT A TRADE. It says the structure resolved downward more often than its pattern-free baseline over the same years. It says nothing about borrow, about whether a name is shortable at all, or about the entry and stop -- and a stock in a Stage 4 breakdown is exactly the kind that can be hard to borrow.

⚠️ AND ITS MARGIN IS THE THINNEST IN THE LEDGER: the CI's lower bound clears the null by 1.06pp, narrower than square-box's 1.16pp on a lift a third the size. The gates certify the margin, not the headline. What makes this one trustworthy despite the thin margin is n=34,216 -- the largest sample of any published short row by a factor of four.

double-bottom.note:

square-box.note:
+0.99pp, CI [+0.35pp, +1.58pp] at n=33,851, against a 30-trial null whose maximum reached -0.81pp.

The smallest published edge in the ledger, and it flipped on evidence: at 279 tickers it was +1.07pp with a CI straddling zero and I wrote it up as a clean null result. At 3,456 tickers the interval excludes zero. ⛔ Its detector needed two corrections before it measured this at all -- the published rules alone matched 46.7% of the universe, and the tilt test that fixes that had to become a RATIO (drift over the box's own depth) because an absolute bound is scale-dependent: 10% of price across a 4-7 week box is a trend, across a 52-week base it is flat. A near-zero null is what makes this small number trustworthy: unlike the double bottom, whose detector finds +4.31pp on pure noise, this one has almost no mechanical edge on random data.

buyable-gap-up.note:
+12.56pp, CI [+10.99, +13.93] at n=5,374, against a 30-trial null whose maximum reached +11.40pp.

⭐ THE ESCALATION RULE WORKING IN THE OTHER DIRECTION. This PASSED its 5-trial screen -- a +12.56pp lift with a CI lower bound of +10.99pp against a null max of +10.42pp -- and FAILED the 30-trial escalation, because the null's upper tail kept climbing: +10.42pp on five draws, +11.40pp on thirty. That is precisely why the escalation runs in one direction only. Stage 4 moved the other way on a wider SAMPLE; this one moved back on a harder NULL, and both are the same discipline.

⚠️ Read the number with its known bias. The detector is an explicit SUBSET of the authors' rule -- their volume gate is not implemented, because it reaches us in two phrasings that differ by a factor of 1.67 and the research note says not to choose between them. A gate we do not apply is a gate whose rejections we do not make, so this measurement includes gap-ups the full rule would refuse.

cheat-3c.note:
-1.10pp, CI [-2.16pp, -0.09pp] at n=6,139, against a 5-trial null whose maximum reached -3.91pp.

⛔⛔ THE ROW THAT EXPOSED A HOLE IN THE GATE. It PUBLISHED with a NEGATIVE lift, because its interval excludes zero (both bounds negative) and its lower bound clears a null that is even more negative. The gate had never checked the sign, and the defect stayed invisible for as long as no structure happened to land in that position. Gate zero now requires a positive lift. The result itself stands as a finding: the best-sourced structure in the build -- nine criteria at high confidence -- does not beat its own baseline.

low-cheat.note:
+2.80pp, CI [+0.83pp, +4.56pp] at n=2,856, against a 30-trial null whose maximum reached +0.40pp.

⚠️⚠️ THE THINNEST RESULT IN THE LEDGER, AND THE ONE TO READ MOST CAREFULLY. Its CI's lower bound clears the null by 0.43pp -- less than half the next-narrowest margin (stage-4 at 1.06pp) -- and its interval is wide: [+0.83, +4.56] spans more than five-fold. That width is n=2,856, the smallest sample of any published row and roughly a twelfth of stage-4's. A structure this rare cannot buy a tight interval, and the gates passed it on the pessimistic end rather than the point estimate, which is exactly what they are for. Treat it as the weakest published claim here, not as a +2.80pp edge.

⭐ WHAT SAVES IT IS A NEAR-ZERO NULL. Thirty rounds of shuffled data produced at best +0.40pp, so this detector has almost no mechanical edge on noise -- unlike ema-crossback, whose null reproduces three-quarters of its much larger headline. Whatever is here is small and is not the detector fooling itself.

⛔ AND IT SHARES A DETECTOR WITH THE 3-C CHEAT, by design: Minervini's framing is positional, so the two are one implementation with one band moved, rather than two detectors with a second authority over every rule they share. The 3-C is measured separately and is NOT published; that these two sit on opposite sides of the bar is a result about where in a base the entry is taken, not about two different patterns.

ema-crossback.note:
+12.94pp, CI [+12.12pp, +13.72pp] at n=18,705, against a 30-trial null whose maximum reached +9.65pp.

⭐⭐ THE FIRST PUBLISHED ROW IN THIS LIBRARY THAT NO HOUSE WROTE DOWN. Every other published structure traces to a published author; this one is ours end to end. The 15-source corpus contains no Kell material at all, so there is no sentence to quote and no threshold to cite -- the 60% prior advance, the 30-bar window and the 5-bar reclaim recency were SWEPT on the real universe, not chosen. It is held to exactly the same bar as Darvas and clears it.

⛔⛔ READ THE NULL BEFORE THE LIFT. The null maximum here is +9.65pp -- by far the largest of any published row (Darvas +1.10pp, square-box -0.81pp). That means this detector reproduces roughly three-quarters of its headline number on RANDOM data: the mechanical edge of 'buy after a pullback in something that has already advanced 60%' is most of what +12.94pp measures. What the gates certify is the MARGIN -- the CI's lower bound clears the null by 2.47pp -- not the headline. A reader who takes +12.94pp as the edge has taken about four times the edge that was demonstrated.

⚠️ AND IT IS ONE LEG OF A TWO-LEG SETUP. Our own playbook trades this both ways; the short leg needs a rejection at the underside of the averages 'or VWAP', which a completed daily bar cannot express. This number is for the long leg alone, on daily bars, and says nothing about the half we did not implement.
